This script builds the article's four tables from the data with [{gtsummary}](https://www.danieldsjoberg.com/gtsummary/): Table 1, the two cohorts' characteristics, and Tables 2 to 4, each outcome before and after the visit within every subgroup. The Stata code made none of them. On this site the tables are shown filled with the article's printed values ([Published results](published_results.qmd) and its pages for [engagement](published_engagement.qmd), [retention](published_retention.qmd) and [viral suppression](published_suppression.qmd)), laid out by the same functions; the script itself writes HTML copies to `tables/`, which is never committed.

::: {.Rcode title="Source code"}
The full R script is available at:

-   [`R/tables.R`](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/Harris-Health-RUSH/blob/main/R/tables.R)

This R script file is itself reliant on the following helper files:

-   [`R/setup.R`](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/Harris-Health-RUSH/blob/main/R/setup.R)
-   [`R/functions.R`](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/Harris-Health-RUSH/blob/main/R/functions.R)

The code sections below are imported directly from that script when this page is rendered.
:::


## One row per patient

The long data have two rows per patient; a table of patients needs one. Selecting the patient number and the characteristics, which are the same in both of a patient's rows, and keeping distinct rows gives one row per patient in each cohort.

The control sheet has no years since diagnosis. The controls are the same patients as the study cohort, with the same patient numbers, so their group is joined from the study cohort. The years workbook holds years from diagnosis to the RUSH-era index visit, so that is the value the controls' column shows.

```{r}
#| label: define-patient-characteristics
#| eval: false
```

## Table 1 counts {#count-table-1}

For each characteristic, the number and column percentage of patients in each category, in each cohort, by `count_categories()`, then the two cohorts side by side. The article's Table 1 pairs each RUSH-era year with the pre-RUSH year in the same position (2009 with 2004), so the years are joined by position rather than by value. The controls' years since diagnosis are those joined in the previous step.

The rows are text, already formatted, because `format_table_1()` lays out text: that is what lets the same function show the article's printed values on the website.

```{r}
#| label: count-table-1
#| eval: false
```

## Tables 2 to 4 rows

For each outcome (engagement, retention, and viral suppression with missing as not suppressed) and each category of each characteristic: the patients with both values and the number and percentage with the outcome before and after the visit, counted by `count_pairs()`; and the odds ratio for the visit with its 95% confidence interval and P value from the conditional logistic regression. A category's odds ratio is the within-category effect of [4. RUSH-era models](04_fit_rush_era_models.qmd#the-effect-within-each-category) (the original code's `lincom`), and the Total row's is the effect of the visit from the model without interactions ([4. RUSH-era models](04_fit_rush_era_models.qmd#the-effect-of-the-visit)). The intervals and P values are Wald ones, the same kind for every row, and they are the ones the article prints: each printed interval matches the Wald interval worked out from its row (decision issue [#5](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/Harris-Health-RUSH/issues/5)). For paired data the odds ratio itself is the ratio of the two kinds of discordant pair, as McNemar's odds ratio is ([Methodological background](methodological_background.qmd#mcnemars-test)); only the interval and P value would differ from McNemar's.

A category in which no patient got worse has an infinite odds ratio. The model returns only a very large number there, with no usable interval or P value, so the row prints "∞" and "-", as the article's Table 4 does. No McNemar test is run for the tables.

The test across categories, the article's χ² column, is the interaction test from the same script, shown once per characteristic. The article's χ² values fit tests with one fewer degree of freedom than categories, which this test has; whether it is the exact statistic the article used is part of [#5](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/Harris-Health-RUSH/issues/5).
